candidate.title: Mod in a helper process over a synchronous pipe

retainedClasses.reason: these trials host no class loader

candidateDelta.reason: every candidate is its own process here, so there is no shared control to subtract

failures.detail: the mod returned its rejection value
the mod process refused an unknown entry point
the host kept running and reported that it survived the mod process ended without answering
the host kept running and reported that it survived the mod ending itself
the harness killed a host that never announced readiness within 3 seconds

safety.maintainedUnsafeDetail: a pipe and a child process are safe standard library operations

operability.diagnostics: the mod's own standard error is separate from the game's, and its exit status survives it
operability.debugWorkflow: the mod can be attached to, restarted, or run under a different debugger than the game
operability.crashAttribution: the operating system attributes the crash to the mod process by construction

isolation.detail: a mod whose body fails: the host kept running and reported that it survived the mod process ended without answering. A mod that ends its own process: the host kept running and reported that it survived the mod ending itself

abiEvolution.detail: the host read contract version 1 and refused the absent entry point before calling it; the contract is the wire protocol, which can carry its own version and refuse an unknown opcode without loading anything

deviations.summary: these trials host no JVM, so the measured cost is the mod-execution boundary alone; reaching it from the game costs what ADG-1 measured, and the two add
the process candidate is measured unbatched, one synchronous request per call, because that is what a hook needs; batching would amortize the round trip but cannot make a hook's answer arrive in time
memory is the sum of two processes sampled at the same boundary by two collectors, so it is a close total rather than one reading
